questions.q: What does the Eventstream canvas's Filter node do?
options: Functionally the same as a KQL where clause, but runs on the stream itself before data lands anywhere
Only works after data has already been ingested
Deletes an entire Eventstream permanently
Converts streaming data into a batch file
questions.explain: Events that fail the filter never get written at all, which can reduce storage and downstream compute cost.

questions.q: What is the Manage Fields node the no-code equivalent of?
options: KQL's project and extend — choosing which fields survive, renaming, or changing type
KQL's summarize by
KQL's join kind=leftouter
A Fabric Warehouse stored procedure
questions.explain: It reshapes fields before an event ever reaches a destination, just like project/extend do after landing.

questions.q: What does the Group By transformation node compute?
options: An aggregate — count, sum, average — grouped by a key, directly on the canvas, the same idea as summarize by
A join between two unrelated streams
A watermark tolerance setting
A KQL Database's storage partition
questions.explain: It's usually paired with a Window node so the grouping also has a time boundary.

questions.q: What does the Join transformation node do on the Eventstream canvas?
options: Combines two streams using a matching key within a time window — the streaming equivalent of KQL's join kind=leftouter
Merges every field from every stream with no matching logic
Only works on data already stored in a KQL Database
Deletes duplicate events from a single stream
questions.explain: This happens before either stream lands in storage, unlike a KQL join which runs against already-landed data.

questions.q: Why would filtering noisy events out in-stream be cheaper than filtering them with a KQL query after they've landed?
options: Events that fail an in-stream filter are never written at all, so storage and downstream compute are spent only on useful data
In-stream filtering is always slower, so this isn't actually true
KQL queries are free regardless of how much data they scan
There's no cost difference between the two approaches
questions.explain: Filtering after landing still pays the cost of storing and scanning the noisy data first.
